requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
The initial-bundle and cycle/transitivity obligations are implemented and tested. Two of the separate read paths that must supply definitions have no test of that behavior, which is a gap. The finding is borderline, because those two paths use the same helper call as the paths that are tested.

**Obligations**
1. Each definition referenced by the subject or a contributed source contributes its complete fenced declaration, including the phrase option.
2. Definitions referenced by those definitions are included transitively, without duplicates and without nontermination on cycles.
3. When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same complete transitive set is supplied to the model.
4. That set is recorded before a submission is accepted.

**Code**
- **Obligations 1 and 2, initial bundle.**
  - `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs) builds the mandatory sources. It then calls `definition_inputs`, passing the subject text.
  - `definition_inputs` calls `terms::dependencies` and turns each name into an `InputSelector::Definition` through `source_input`.
  - `terms::direct_references` collects term references from the subject text and from every contributed input, whether Requirements, Rust comments or Markdown.
  - `terms::close_dependencies` (src/terms.rs) expands to a fixed point using `visited`/`required` sets. That gives no duplicates and no loop on cycles.
  - `InputSelector::resolve` for a definition returns the redacted `raw_lines`, which is the whole fenced declaration with the `:phrase:` line.
- **Obligations 3 and 4.**
  - `additional_definitions` recomputes the closure over the newly read inputs. It filters out definitions already in the inputs or already recorded.
  - `read`, `search`, `structural` and `declared_query` (src/authoring/tools.rs) each call it. Each puts the result in `definitions` and appends it to `ToolDelivery.inputs`.
  - `converse` (src/authoring/mod.rs) puts delivered inputs in `pending`. It calls `record_inputs(&pending)` as soon as the next response arrives, before the submission is parsed.

**Tests**
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (inputs.rs) covers the initial bundle. It uses the cycle value↔unit and checks the two definitions are each present once.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` covers a term referenced by a contributed source.
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` (mod.rs) covers the transitive cyclic set, the full text with phrase, delivery before submission, and recording. It uses the file+item read form.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` covers the item read form and recording.
- `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` covers `ripgrep`.
- `ast_grep_returns_innermost_nodes_of_the_language_and_reports_failures` covers `ast_grep` with a rule.

**Gaps**
- `declared_query` (tools.rs, ast_grep `query` form) carries an {impl} for this requirement. It is a separate path that computes and delivers additional definitions. Its only test, `ast_grep_queries_run_declared_queries_and_return_their_sites`, has no {test} reference to this requirement. Its project has no terminology, and it never asserts on `definitions`.
- The line-range form of `habeas` in `read` is also a separate path that calls `additional_definitions`. Its test (the `eof` call in `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms`) checks only `inputs`, never `definitions`.

Each path that supplies definitions along its own route needs a test of that outcome. These two have none.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
